newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed, volume jumps in Bogota.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed, volume jumps in Bogota.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed after volume in Bogota surged to a 1996 record of 22.3 billion pesos on the back of heavy trading in Banco de Colombia, the country's second largest bank in terms of assets.
Medellin's IBOMED general price index edged up 0.10 percent to end at 13,666.34 on volume of 1.1 billion pesos, while Bogota's IBB slipped 0.05 percent to close at 869.66.
The Bogota exchange said high volume there had been fuelled by the sale of 47.9 million shares in Banco de Bogota.

The sale, at 435 pesos per share for a total of 20.8 billion pesos, drove Banco de Colombia up 4.81 percent. But it was not factored into the IBB index at the close because it was a "forward" operation due to be completed on October 30.
Brokers said the deal, in which 4.5 percent of the bank's shares changed hands, was believed to involve a cross trade between large shareholders.
Arfin, a rarely-traded credit company, was also heavily traded in Bogota, accounting for 675.1 million of total volume.
Closely watched Cementos Diamante rose 0.36 percent in Bogota to close at 4,250 pesos per share.
Other gains in Bogota were made Banco de Bogota, which rose 0.16 percent to end at 5,940 pesos.
The ordinary shares of blue-chip Banco Ganadero slipped 0.35 percent, ending at 282 pesos per share, while brewer Bavaria edged down 0.22 percent to end at 3,941.
Winners in Medellin were led by Cementos Caribe of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueo conglomerate, which rose 2.44 percent to end at 4,200 pesos a share.
